 Print Gautam Gambhir scored 72 and shared a solid partnership with Rahul Dravid, who made 66. (AFP Photo) WELLINGTON: New Zealand has always remained a tricky frontier for India. It's been 17 years since India last won a Test match in New Zealand. Even India's famous win at Seddon Park in Hamilton in 2009, which sealed a memorable series victory for the MS Dhoni-led side, came 33 years after the previous Test series win in New Zealand. Kyle Mills , part of the New Zealand squad for the Hamilton fixture, vividly, but not fondly, remembers the game as his last outing for the Black Caps in whites. "I remember that Test very well. That Test match was the epitome of the Rahul Dravid ‘Wall’. He batted beautifully and really dug in, batting us into submission. That was actually my last Test match, so not fond memories," Mills recalled in an interview with TOI. Watch Shreyas Iyer on India's series win, bowling brilliance, captaincy challenges and more The Kiwi seamer, who took a solitary wicket in the match, still remembers getting Team India head coach Gautam Gambhir out leg before wicket, but he had overstepped, which gave the southpaw an early reprieve. Mills feels it could have been a different story had they taken the early wicket, but it wasn't meant to be. "I actually got Gambhir out LBW; well, it was out, it was absolutely dead out, but my front foot was over the line, and Simon Taufel was the umpire and called me for a no ball, and then I was gutted because it would have been great to get an early wicket, and then who knows how the game would have progressed," says Mills. Gambhir scored 72 and partnered solidly with Rahul Dravid, and the two set a solid platform for the Little Master Sachin Tendulkar to dominate from. Tendulkar scored a brilliant 160, and his 260-ball essay was enough to bat the hosts out of the game. "Rahul Dravid was amazing in that Test match, so was Sachin Tendulkar. You kind of think about some of the players you had in that series... Zaheer Khan was playing; they're generational cricketing greats, (Virender) Sehwag played that Test, (VVS) Laxman was also there. India had a brilliant cricket team during that period and potentially played as well... just a brilliant cricket team," adds Mills. Join conversation

(AFP Photo) The fixture turned out to be a cruel ending for Mills in more ways than one, as he also conceded the winning runs off Gambhir's bat in the second innings when India stormed home without losing a wicket. The former India opener now returns to the familiar territory but with a different challenge, and without the bat in hand. For Mills, Gambhir remains the "tough competitor" unwilling to drop an inch. "He's always a tough competitor on the field, without question. No jokes were going around at all because he was always business on the field, a tough cricketer. Post-cricket, he got into politics and became a leader. He is obviously a great tactician, was a wonderful player, very professional across all facets of the game, and a tough taskmaster as well," concludes Mills.
